en.value: In a optical fibre cable, the signal is propagated along

english.explanation: Optical fiber is a technology used to transmit data by sending short light pulses along a long fiber which is typically made of glass or plastic.  Total internal reflection of light is used in the fiber optical cable. This effect is used in optical fibres to confine light in the core. Light travel through the fibre core, bouncing back and forth off the boundary between the core and cladding.  Cladding is the outer optical material surrounding the core having reflecting index lower than core. It helps to keep the light within the core throughout the phenomena of total internal reflection.

en.value: The average lifetime of an atom in metastable state is

english.explanation: The metastable state is the state which lies between the ground state and excited state. The atom in the ground state absorbs some energy and goes to the excited state. From an excited state, it loses some energy and comes to a metastable state. The lifetime of the metastable state is 10–3 sec.  A metastable state is one which has a mean life time of the order of 10–3 s or more (much larger than 10–8 s). Some atomic systems such as chromium neon etc. posses metastable states.

english.explanation: Planck's constant defines the behavior of particles and waves on atomic scale. It is denoted by 'h'.  The energy and frequency in the case of photon energy are directly proportional to each other and hence planck's constant is the constant of proportionality between them. Its value is 6.62676 × 10–34 Joule-second. E h = ν  The unit is same as that of angular momentum. Its SI unit is joule-second and CGS unit is erg-seconds.

en.value: In a photoelectric effect experiment at a frequency above cut off, the number of electrons ejected is proportional to

options.prompt: the frequency of the incident light

english.explanation: The photoelectric effect is the phenomenon where electrons are emitted from a material when it is exposed to light.  The photoelectric effect does not occur at all if the frequency of the light source is below a certain value. This value which is characteristic of the kind of metal surface used in the experiment, is called cutoff frequency. Above the cutoff frequency each photon of light carries, sufficient energy to eject an electron. Since each photon can eject one electron, increasing the intensity of light increases the number of photon reaching the material's surface and consequently increases the number of electrons ejected. So, the number of electron ejected in the photoelectric effect is directly proportional to the intensity of light.

Some types of crystalline structure that exhibit the piezoelectric effect include quartz, topaz and Rochelle salt etc.

en.value: Thermocouple consists of

english.explanation: A thermocouple is a temperature sensor that operates based on the principle of the seebeck effect. It is a device composed of two dissimilar metal wires or conductors that are joined together at one end to form a junction. The other ends of the wires are typically connected to a measuring instrument or a control system.  When there is a temperature difference between the two junctions of a thermocouple, it generates a voltage known as the thermoelectric voltage. It is directly proportional to the temperature difference between the two junctions. By measuring this voltage, the temperature at one of the junctions (known as measurement or hot junction) can be inferred relative to the temperature at the other junction (known as the reference of cold junction).

en.value: Superconductors when cooled below TC undergo a transition to the following state

english.explanation: A superconductors is defined as a substance that offers no resistance to the electric current when it becomes colder than a critical temperature. For example – aluminum, copper oxide, magnesium diboride etc.  When a superconductor is cooled below its critical temperature, it forms cooper pairs - a quantum mechanical phenomenon involving pairs of electrons with opposite momentum and spin. These cooper pairs in addition to zero electrical resistance also generate a perfect cancellation of any external magnetic field within the superconductors. As a result a super conductor exhibits strong diamagnetic properties, actively expelling magnetic field from its interior.

It is the only particle that explain how the fundamental building blocks of matter interact. It is often called the "God particles" because it is significant in subatomic physics.  A boson has the following properties– (i) Nuclei with an even mass number (ii) An integral spin. (iii) Angular momentum in quantum mechanical units of 0 and 1.

en.value: There are regions of energy for which Bloch function solutions of wave equation do not exist. These are called

english.explanation: Bloch theorem states that the electron wave functions in a periodic crystal lattice can be described by Bloch functions, which are a combination of plane waves and periodic functions. It is used to describe the electronic states and energy bands in solids.  There are energy ranges within the crystal structure where Bloch function solutions do not exist. These energy ranges are called forbidden energy or band gaps. It means, that there are no allowed energy levels or wave functions for electrons within those energy ranges. DSSSB PGT 174 YCT

en.value: In superconductors, the energy gap is due to

english.explanation: In superconductors, the energy gap is primarily due to interaction between electron and lattice vibrations which are known as phonons. This interaction is referred to as the electron phonon interaction. These interactions lead to the formation of pairs of electrons called cooper pairs with opposite momentum and spin.  The energy gap in a superconductor refers to the energy difference between the highest filled electron state (located below the gap) and the lowest available empty state (located above the gap) in the superconducting energy spectrum.  This energy gap is a characteristic feature of superconductors and is responsible for their unique properties such as zero electrical resistance and the expulsion of magnetic fields (Meissner effect).

en.value: A diode that has a negative resistance characteristic is the

english.explanation: A tunnel diode (also known as Esaki diode) is a type of semiconductor diode that has negative resistance due to the quantum mechanical effect called tunneling. This feature (negative resistance) makes it useful in oscillator and microwave amplifier applications.  Tunnel diodes are constructed with germanium or gallium arsenide by doping the p and n regions much more heavily than in a conventional rectifier diode. As a result there is no break down effect for reverse voltage and an extremely narrow regions. The extremely narrow depletion region permits electrons to "tunnel" through the pn junction at very low forward bias voltage and the diode acts as a conductor at between point A and B. DSSSB PGT 175 YCT  At point B, the forward voltage begins to develop a barrier and the current begins to decrease as the forward voltage continues to increase. This is the negative resistance region.

In an intrinsic semiconductor, even at rooms temperature, hole-electron pairs are created. When electric field is applied across an intrinsic semiconductor, the current conduction takes place by two processes namely by free electrons and holes.  The free electrons are produced due to the breaking up of some covalent bonds by thermal energy. This process results in a detectable electrical pulse or discharge, which is recorded and used to determine the presence and intensity of the radiation.
